voyage.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
voyage.content: The 8th largest mosque in the world, boasts a total of 82 domes. On Fridays, it is closed to the public and open only for worshippers. You can get there by public bus #54. Make sure to ask the bus driver to tell you when you get there. The public bus stop is 100 m before the mosque and after that is no stop for the next 5 km. The Mosque Centre offers several free tours of the mosque every day. Times vary on a daily b

voyage.name: Qasr Al Watan
voyage.content: Opened to the public in 2019, this is the presidential palace for diplomatic visits. As one would expect from UAE, the palace is very opulent and features great Islamic architecture. Inside you will find a banquet hall, a library, a museum containing diplomatic gifts and several dining outlets.

voyage.name: Qasr al-Hosn
voyage.content: The oldest stone building in Abu Dhabi, this small fort was first constructed in 1761 and served as the royal palace from the late 18th century until 1966. The site can be visited: the ticket allows you to visit the fort itself, the Cultural Foundation, the House of Artisans and enjoy the Bait Al Gahwa (traditional preparation of Arabic coffee).

voyage.name: Corniche Road
voyage.content: The city's main avenue, it curves around the coastline along Abu Dhabi's spectacular waterfront that stretches for miles from the breakwater near Marina Shopping Mall almost up to the Mina Zayed port. The shoreline is lined with a walkway for the entire length, skyscrapers, lovely beaches, parks, and other landscaped areas. There are many activities like go-kart riding, playgrounds and even stages for shows. Come in

voyage.name: Yas Island
voyage.content: It has a Formula 1 race track, Ferrari World (a Ferrari-themed park with the fastest roller coaster in the world), the Warner Bros. World theme park, the SeaWorld Abu Dhabi themepark, Yas Waterworld, a shopping mall and a hotel.

voyage.name: UAE flag pole
voyage.content: At 122 m, this is among the world's tallest flagpoles, and you won't miss the massive UAE flag flying from it. It is on Marina Island across from Marina Mall.

voyage.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
voyage.hours: Sat Sun Tue Wed 10AM-8PM, Thu Fri 10AM-10PM, closed on Mon
voyage.content: Art and civilization museum exhibits artworks from Musée du Louvre and other French collections. Opened in November 2017, the largest art museum in Arabian peninsula with 24000 m2, including 8000 m2 of galleries.

voyage.name: Masdar City
voyage.content: A green city project, open to tourists. Features some unique buildings. Here the UAE try new concepts in reducing energy consumption and environmental impact. You can use podcars here, a still quite rare form of public transport.

voyage.name: Emirates Palace
voyage.content: Even though it's a hotel, Emirates Palace is a very popular tourist attraction. Inside, you'll get to see all the luxury and glamour of one of the most expensive hotels in the world plus, you'll have some picture opportunities. Additionally, you can get to try the very popular Palace Cappuccino, sparkled with 23-karat gold flakes for 75 dirham.

voyage.name: The National Aquarium Abu Dhabi
voyage.content: Home to more than 45,000 animals across 60 different exhibits, this is the Middle East's largest aquarium.

voyage.name: Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital
voyage.content: Covered by TV and media outlets all over the world. Learn everything about falcons and the special meaning of those birds in the UAE. All tours have to be booked in advance.

voyage.name: Etihad Arena
voyage.content: This arena hosts some of the highest-profile events of the year: concerts, comedy shows, and UFC matches.

voyage.name: Abrahamic Family House
voyage.address: Jacques Chirac St - Al Saadiyat Island - Cultural District
voyage.content: The Abrahamic Family House is an interfaith complex on Saadiyat Island. It was inaugurated on 16 February 2023. It features a cultural centre and rooftop garden as well as a mosque, synagogue and church in distinctive and modern architectural styles.

voyage.name: Khalifa Park
voyage.content: The best park by far, built at a cost of US$50 million. It has an aquarium, museum, train, play parks and formal gardens.

voyage.name: Umm Al Emarat Park
voyage.content: It's a vibrant park with a shaded house and a botanical garden. The entrance fee is 10 dirham (April 2022).

voyage.name: Abu Dhabi Cultural Foundation
voyage.content: A landmark in the Emirates, it holds cultural events and workshops throughout the year. It has a well-stocked library, children's programs, art exhibitions, benefits, and other culture-related activities that are the hallmark of any city. It's well worth a look.

voyage.name: Manarat al Saadiyat
voyage.content: An exhibition space and cultural centre with galleries, a theatre and a restaurant, opened in 2009 and with works by contemporary artists from around the world.

voyage.name: UAE Pavilion
voyage.content: Sand dune-inspired exhibition centre designed by Norman Foster.

voyage.name: Lulu Islands
voyage.content: A group of artificial islands, already built just offshore at great expense, but sitting there doing nothing after a tourism venture failed to even start construction.

voyage.name: Reem Island
voyage.content: By the time it is completed, it will be a residential, commercial and educational haven. Reem Island is progressing well, with many skyscrapers being built on the island to facilitate its growing population. The Reem Island skyline has impressive number of tall buildings. However, the north side of the island is still quite sparse. Despite this, there are many facilities available and Reem Island is a good place to l

voyage.name: Lessons
voyage.content: Some hotels also offer dance lessons, aerobics classes, and other physical entertainment.

voyage.name: Desert safari
voyage.content: Trips are a tourist but fun experience. They must be booked ahead, but can often be booked as late as the day before, most hotel receptionists can arrange this for you. Trips start late afternoon and end at night. You will be collected from your hotel and driven to the desert in a 4x4 vehicle. Most packages include a bone-rattling drive over the dunes, a short camel ride, a mediocre Arabic buffet and a belly dancer.

voyage.name: Shopping
voyage.content: The official sport of the Emirates, and Abu Dhabi offers plenty of opportunity in this area.

voyage.name: Helicopter Tour
voyage.content: Board a 6-seater Eurocopter EC130 B4 and Discover Abu Dhabi from a birds' eye view with Falcon Aviation Services. Tours operate daily from 9AM to 5PM the Marina Mall Terminal. Reservations recommended (tours can be booked on an individual or private basis).

voyage.name: Abu Dhabi Mall
voyage.content: A three-story shopping mall.

voyage.name: Marina Mall
voyage.content: Has a musical fountain and ceilings that thunder and rain.

voyage.name: Yas Mall
voyage.content: Opened in 2014 next to Ferrari World on Yas Island. This is the biggest mall in Abu Dhabi and the 16th biggest mall in the world. It has the first Lego store in the UAE. It is connected to Ferrari World.

voyage.name: Al Wahda Mall
voyage.content: A large, modern mall. Shops are high-end, the food court is extensive, and a large LuLu Hypermart in the basement.

voyage.name: Khalidiyah Mall
voyage.address: Mubarak bin Mohammed St, Al Khalidiyah W9 area
voyage.content: Khalidiya Mall is small but a nice place to visit. The droll fashion stores may grip you for maybe several seconds, but then the obvious lack of things to do kicks in. However, the food court is popular, alongside New York Fries, Chili's, a Dunkin' Donuts, and Baskin Robbins. Downstairs there is an extortionate Krispy Kreme and Starbucks, and a what looks to be an Indian/Arabian cuisine restaurant, which seems good b

voyage.name: Shams Boutik
voyage.content: A growing mall built around the community of Reem Island. It contains a growing number of good shops, including a supermarket, three restaurants, several fast food restaurants on the first floor, a café, a kids play area, a nail salon, a bookstore and more. Despite, this, it is placed in an area that isn't usually busy, and is not very popular.

voyage.name: The Mall - World Trade Center Abu Dhabi & WTC Souk
voyage.address: Khalifa bin Zayed the First St crossing Sheik Rachid bin Saeed St, Al Danah
voyage.content: Nice architecture in the Mall and Souk.

voyage.name: Fish Market
voyage.content: A fish market with restaurants attached, where you can have your choice of fresh fish cooked with your choice of seasoning, sauce and accompaniments.

voyage.name: The Resto Pinoy, Al Khalidiyah Branch
voyage.address: Al Khalidiya - Zayed The First St
voyage.content: A Filipino restaurant

voyage.name: Ghalib Restaurant
voyage.address: Khalidiya D - Building No.3960, Sheikh Zayed 1st Street - W Corniche Rd

voyage.name: Nalas Aappakadai Restaurant
voyage.content: Speciality for Aappam & excellent South Indian food from the Chettinad cuisine, Chinese & Tandoor

voyage.name: NOOG Burger
voyage.address: Sheikh Rashid Bin Saeed St - Zone 1 - E22

voyage.name: Manzo Sushi & Sliders Restaurant
voyage.address: Sheikh Rashid Bin Saeed St - Zone 1 - E22

voyage.name: Philippine House Restaurant
voyage.address: Abu Dhabi Muay Thai - Fatima Bint Mubarak St - Zone 1

voyage.name: Aroma Spicy Restaurant
voyage.content: An Indian restaurant

voyage.name: Anand Vegetarian Restaurant
voyage.content: This is a pure veg Gujarati (North Indian) style restaurant. The demand for Puri Bhaji, a deep-fried bread and potato and chickpea dish, is so great that you will have to wait your turn but it's worth it. There is a special part for ladies and families. Friday lunch has sweets and as much Puri as you want. Sometimes you will have to wait for 10 min to get a roti.

voyage.name: The Olive Branch
voyage.hours: Open 24 hours daily serving buffet and an à la carte menu buffet serving times: breakfast 6-10:30AM, lunch 12:30-3:30PM, dinner 7-11PM
voyage.content: Mafraq’s all day restaurant serves up fresh Mediterranean cuisine borrowing influence from various regions, including France, Spain and Turkey. The buffet is prepared with the freshest of ingredients and the interior décor is equally breezy and funky.

voyage.name: Hunter’s B&R
voyage.hours: Open daily from noon to 2:30AM with food served throughout
voyage.content: A modern bar with green brick walls, solid wood tables and numerous flat screen TVs showing sports. God for after work drinks, or an evening with friends, Hunter’s B&R offers a casual environment with a social buzz.

voyage.name: Rimal
voyage.content: Rimal Asian fusion bar serves up oriental dishes in an authentic atmosphere with a modern edge. Taste the delicious flavours from Korea, China and Japan in this Asian inspired outlet, complete with Sake and signature cocktails.

voyage.name: Oasis Courtyard
voyage.hours: Daily from noon to 9PM with food served throughout
voyage.content: This poolside bar and restaurant serves drinks under the sun and a wide selection of snacks. The swim-up bar in the pool offers refreshment. Shisha is also available.

voyage.name: The Burlington Grill
voyage.content: The hotel’s grill restaurant serves grilled meat and seafood steaks. Choose from an array of starters and salads including crab cakes, goats cheese tartlets and American-style Louisiana fish gumbo. Has al fresco dining on the terrace and an aperitif bar.

voyage.name: Hemingway's
voyage.content: The main restaurant has a good Tex-Mex menu, a wide selection of beer on tap and features live music in the evening. Jazz Bar. The second venue, has great food and a good jazz band. The band normally changes every six months or so, but the quality is consistent and they take requests. The bartenders normally put on a show by tossing bottles around while mixing a mean cocktail. The third place is Cinnabar, a nightclub

voyage.name: The Captain's Arms
voyage.content: Traditional British pub located in the hotel courtyard. The pub features traditional food and a great selection of beer on tap. The large terrace is great during the cooler months of the year. A typical hang-out for the expat crowd, but try to get there early, as it attracts a large after-work crowd.

voyage.name: Wakataua Terrace
voyage.content: A Polynesian-themed cocktail bar located at the far end of the courtyard, right on the water. The cocktails are amazing. The Navy Grog is highly recommended. It has a nice view at night over the water.

voyage.name: Rock Bottom
voyage.content: One of the most popular night club locations in all of Abu Dhabi. It stays open later than most venues, and is cheaper. If you get there early enough, they have decent food you can enjoy in the restaurant area. They have both a live band and an excellent DJ, along with black lights and lasers. There is a hot dog stand later in the night, providing some delicious drunk snacks. Thursday nights can get extremely crowded

voyage.name: Havana Club
voyage.content: The grand hotel is a must-see in Abu Dhabi and the actual club is nicely decorated, comfortable, has great service, a balcony overlooking the hotel grounds, and provides a fun time with great music and very colorful laser shows.

voyage.name: Sax
voyage.content: Sax is a beautifully decorated club with sleek black marble floors, two bars, a DJ, and depending on the time, a jazz band. The club is often very loud and very dark with little more than lasers lighting the room. It's not a place to go if you expect to talk at all, at least not on a weekend night. Collared shirts are required for men, and sneakers usually do not pass the bouncers either. It is not uncommon to have t

voyage.name: PJ's
voyage.content: A 'traditional' Irish pub, boasting brunch buffets and a long happy hour. The majority of the guests are usually British, American or Australian. There is something entertaining going on every day of the week, from 'Quiz Night' to 'Ladies Night'. If you want to start drinking early, this is the place to go. No one will bat an eye if you order beer with brunch, and you will probably find yourself staying for more than

voyage.name: Trader Vic's
voyage.content: A famous cocktail bar/restaurant. The flattering lighting, interesting menu, and soft but fun island music make this a great place for a date or hanging out with people you actually want to talk to. The cocktail menu is pages long, and ordering a complicated fruity concoction is a must. The drinks may be a little on the expensive side at times, but they're reasonably strong and the atmosphere is great. There is a hap

voyage.name: 49ers
voyage.content: A steakhouse/bar. It is often quoted as "more of a meat market than a steakhouse" because of its reputation for prostitution. It is uncomfortable and the men in the bar will probably assume you are for sale. The Novotel Hotel and the Sands Hotel are also notorious for their nightclubs that men frequent when looking to purchase a date for the night.

voyage.name: Mardi Gras
voyage.content: A small restaurant/bar. Its ambiance reminds one of a spa. The service is good, the drinks are reasonable, and the food is tasty. The band often leaves much to be desired, and the DJ is worse.

voyage.name: The Yacht Club
voyage.address: King Abdullah Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street
voyage.content: A gorgeous view of the sunset over the marina if you sit outside. Inside has a very modern, minimalistic feel. The cocktails are delicious, but expensive.

voyage.name: Rabbit Hutch
voyage.content: The dedicated British Embassy Rabbit Hutch is a nice pub with music, a pool and a small play area for children. Although you have to know someone on the inside to get into this rather exclusive pub, the British friends and the refreshing pool is definitely worth it. They do all sorts of drinks, but don't ask for a martini, on the rocks, shaken not stirred.

voyage.name: Lebinese Flower
voyage.content: Great food and nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: Arkadia
voyage.content: Popular nightclub.

voyage.name: Harvesters Pub
voyage.content: A great English pub, free pool, dart boards, multiple screens showing sports, excellent fish and chips as well as other English style meals, friendly staff, English band every night except Sundays, quiz nights every Tuesday and possibly the cheapest beer in town.

voyage.name: Grand Continental Flamingo
voyage.content: This is the hotel the taxis cannot find. A 2-story atrium, quiet setting, rooms with bidet, bath and over-bath shower and wide screen TVs all contribute to a pleasant stay. Only the dimness of the lighting and the overdone carpets in the room lets it down. The bath towels are also a bit small.

voyage.name: Park Inn Abu Dhabi Yas Island
voyage.content: Clean rooms, excellent service and friendly staff. The restaurant is a great option for dinner.

voyage.name: Aloft Abu Dhabi
voyage.content: Trendy hotel with cool dark colors, attractive young hotel desk clerks, relatively small rooms (beds are comfortable though), good restaurant and lobby bar, fantastic outdoor lounge on the roof, and half-empty disco next door. Great if there's a convention, but it's walkable to nothing else. Car or taxi is needed to get just about anywhere. Maybe when the nearby residential/commercial development is ready in a few ye

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza
voyage.content: Luxury hotel for a little less money than the Hilton or both of Les Meridiens. Best Asian and Italian restaurants in the city are on the ground level. Service can be a little slow, bed is comfortable. There is a rooftop bar upstairs which seems always empty. Maybe more a 4½-star hotel, not a 5-star. You can sometimes get a "car" instead of taxi to take you places, for not much more than the taxi.

voyage.name: Beach Rotana Hotel and Towers
voyage.content: Marble everywhere sums it up. The club rooms are worth it if you are having to pay full rates for the classic rooms in the main older hotel. They are not much bigger but the use of the Club Lounge is valuable if you are going to be in the hotel a lot and the TV arrangements are more modern, the view wide. It now looks over the hectic construction on the new artificial islands across the creek.

voyage.name: Eastern Mangroves Hotel & Spa
voyage.content: 222 rooms and suites, infinity swimming pool, meeting and event facilities, wedding facilities.

voyage.name: Emirates Palace
voyage.content: Built at an estimated cost of US$3 billion, this was by many accounts the world's most expensive hotel to build, with oodles of gold and marble plating every available surface. The scale of everything is gargantuan — you need directions just to find your way from the gate to the lobby. The hotel feels like it's straight out of Las Vegas, minus the slot machines. To visit the Palace, you will need a reservation

voyage.name: Hilton Abu Dhabi
voyage.content: One of the older hotels in Abu Dhabi, but kept in good shape and renovated. There is a huge Hiltonia beach, pool and spa complex across the street (free for guests), and a small gym in hotel. "Plus" rooms face the sea but are otherwise identical to normal ones. It's a fair distance from the city center, which is both good (no construction noise) and bad (virtually nothing within walking distance). There are shuttle s

voyage.name: InterContinental Abu Dhabi
voyage.content: One of the long-time prestige hotels. Expensive but occasional Internet deals on the hotel independent booking websites are worth it if you are willing to pay upfront online. The lobby is huge. Rooms seem a little 1980s with their decor (way too many mirrors) but beds are comfortable and the views are nice. Gym and fine (but expensive) restaurants. Abu Dhabi locals frequent the hotel piano lounge and the Brazilian re

voyage.name: Le Méridien Abu Dhabi
voyage.content: Tell the taxi driver "Lee Meridien" and he will not confuse it with Royal Meridien. Best amenity is the Meridien Village, an outdoor garden filled with restaurants and pubs, and on Thursday nights during the cooler months, a hangout for literally thousands of expats.

voyage.name: Le Royal Méridien Abu Dhabi
voyage.content: Beautiful views of the gulf and Corniche, comfortable beds, lots of restaurants and bars (very pricey). Service is very good, but things like bringing a welcoming fruit plate to your room (formerly common in 5-star hotels) are extras now. Rotating restaurant at top, and a somewhat hidden nightclub on the 4th floor for dealings on the dark side. Sometimes can get real good deals on internet booking sites. They hold a

voyage.name: Park Inn by Radisson Abu Dhabi, Yas Island
voyage.content: Overlooks the golf course and F1 Circuit. It has 397 rooms comprising suites and business class. All day dining restaurant, Italian restaurant, Persian restaurant, lobby bar, and pool bar.
